description: Magic item definitions with level-appropriate availability and progressive bonuses

weapons.name: Dagger +1
weapons.description: A well-worn blade with a faint blue-silver sheen along its edge that wasn't there when it was made. The grip leather is cracked from use, but the edge holds in a way plain iron never does.

weapons.name: Shortsword +1
weapons.description: The crossguard is pitted and the pommel has been replaced with something mismatched, but the blade carries a restless blue-silver cast that surfaces at the edge in low light. Whatever was done to it, it wasn't done here.

weapons.name: Longsword +1
weapons.description: A longsword worn smooth at the grip from years of handling, the fuller scratched and the hilt-wrap replaced more than once. A faint blue-silver luminescence sits at the very edge — not a reflection, something held in the steel.

weapons.name: Greatsword +1
weapons.description: A two-handed blade marked with the long use its weight demands — one face holds shallow nicks that no whetstone ever fully removed. The steel faintly shears blue-silver near the tip, as if the enchantment settled there and has nowhere else to go.

weapons.name: Battleaxe +1
weapons.description: The haft has been resocketed with cord and a copper ferrule; the head itself is older, its cheeks showing a thin blue-silver wash that seems to move slightly when the light doesn't. The enchantment sat in the iron before the haft was lost.

weapons.name: Rapier +1
weapons.description: A narrow blade from a culture that valued geometry over mass — the ricasso stamped with a maker's mark in script that predates any Kethara record. A cold blue-silver sheen runs the length of the forte, too precise to be a surface treatment.

weapons.name: Shortbow +1
weapons.description: Compact and asymmetric, shaped by hands for a slightly different body type than most Verge archers — the lower limb is shorter than the upper by an inch that can't be accident. The heartwood holds a faint blue-silver cast that appears only when the bow is at full draw.

weapons.name: Longbow +1
weapons.description: A tall stave bow with two generations of weatherproofing worked into the grain, the grip wrapped and rewrapped in hide from something local. At full draw, a faint blue-silver shimmer traces the belly of both limbs — not heat, not flex. Something else.

weapons.name: Longsword +2
weapons.description: The steel has a depth to it that ordinary iron doesn't — a cold violet light lives at the edge, visible even in full daylight, too even to be reflection and too faint to illuminate anything. The blade has been sharpened many times; the enchantment has not diminished.

weapons.name: Greatsword +2
weapons.description: Massive and scarred across one flat from an impact that would have shattered a lesser blade — the damage is old, unmended, almost deliberate. A cold violet edge-light runs both cutting faces in a line so consistent it looks less like enchantment and more like a structural property of whatever the steel is.

weapons.name: Battleaxe +2
weapons.description: A wide-cheeked head on a replaced haft, the iron dense and cold to the touch in a way unrelated to ambient temperature. Cold violet light pools faintly in the beard and along the bit — not a coating, something that originates inside the metal.

weapons.name: Rapier +2
weapons.description: The blade narrows to a geometry that shouldn't hold at this gauge — whatever process made it was not a forge anyone on the Verge has seen. Cold violet light runs the needle-point and traces the fuller back to the shoulder, faint and absolutely still.

weapons.name: Longsword +3
weapons.description: Every settlement on the Verge is younger than the wear on this blade — the pommel engraving is half-gone and the languet fitted by someone who didn't know the original hilt geometry. A deep violet aura breathes along the edge, slow enough to make you doubt you saw it move.

weapons.name: Greatsword +3
weapons.description: A blade from a time before the current settlements, its origin script completely unfamiliar even to Verathi archivists who have seen most things. The deep violet aura that drifts from the edge distorts the air immediately around the steel in a way that is subtle enough to be doubted until it isn't.

armor.name: Leather Armor +1
armor.description: Panels of hide from two different animals, re-stitched with waxed cord where the original binding failed — the enchantment is in the leather itself, not the work, and a faint blue-silver sheen catches where the hide was thinnest.

armor.name: Chain Shirt +1
armor.description: Close-woven rings in two gauges that shouldn't mix this well — the heavier rings at the shoulders are a repair, but whoever made them matched the pattern. Under direct light a pale blue-silver sheen moves across the links in a wave that has no visible source.

armor.name: Breastplate +1
armor.description: A pressed-steel chest with a replaced buckle assembly and padding re-stuffed with local materials — the original fitter is long gone, but the plate was shaped for a body close enough. A blue-silver luminescence sits at the shaped edges, uneasy against the scratched utilitarian steel.

armor.name: Half Plate +1
armor.description: Full coverage from mismatched sources — the pauldrons are a different origin entirely, fastened with strapping that was clearly improvised but has outlasted the original. The blue-silver sheen crosses all of it indiscriminately, as if the enchantment doesn't recognise the seams.

armor.name: Chain Mail +1
armor.description: Thousands of rings, most original, a noticeable minority replaced in slightly different iron — the repair work is competent but visible if you look for it. The whole mass holds a faint blue-silver cast that makes the suit look cleaned even when it isn't.

armor.name: Plate Mail +1
armor.description: A full suit with three visibly different steel qualities across its panels — whoever assembled this sourced what they could. The articulation at the elbows and knees is loud, but the blue-silver sheen that crosses every plate and rivet seems unbothered by the patchwork.

armor.name: Chain Shirt +2
armor.description: The links are all one gauge here, and close inspection reveals they were never riveted — drawn and butted in a method no current Verge smith uses, the joins holding by some property of the metal itself. A cold violet light breathes steadily through the weave.

armor.name: Breastplate +2
armor.description: Shaped from a single pressed piece without seam or join in a way that would require a press no current Verge foundry has. Dents and scratches testify to real use, but the cold violet light that edges every contoured line doesn't waver.

armor.name: Half Plate +2
armor.description: Heavy plate in a fitting style unfamiliar to local armourers — the articulation at the hip uses a pivot geometry they haven't produced here. Cold violet light sits at every shaped edge, making the scratches and field repairs look like damage to something that shouldn't exist.

armor.name: Plate Mail +2
armor.description: A complete suit in a consistent style that marks it as one person's commission rather than assembled piecemeal, though that person is long gone. Cold violet light edges the fluting on every plate, and the suit sits fractionally cooler than the air around it.

armor.name: Plate Mail +3
armor.description: Every plate bears micro-engraving in a script no active culture recognises — it covers the inner faces where no one would see it, which means it was put there for a reason that wasn't decoration. A deep violet aura drifts at the edges and seems to absorb rather than cast light, the slow pulse of it slightly wrong against the breath.

shields.name: Shield +1
shields.description: Banded wood with a replaced iron boss — the original boss was pried off or lost, and the replacement is heavier and slightly off-centre. A blue-silver sheen moves along the rim in a direction counter to how light falls on it.

shields.name: Shield +2
shields.description: A steel-faced round shield whose facing has been worked into a pattern by someone who understood what they were enchanting — the surface geometric, deliberate, the cold violet light it holds running along every line of the design as if the pattern was the point.

wondrous.name: Cloak of Protection
wondrous.description: A travelling cloak in heavy undyed wool, the hem unravelled and re-hemmed unevenly — it has been worn for years by someone for whom this was their only cloak. A restless blue-silver sheen moves at the edges when the wearer is still, as if the garment is still walking.

wondrous.name: Ring of Protection
wondrous.description: A plain band in an alloy that reads as silver until held — then the weight is wrong, too dense for its size, the interior polished to a mirror finish that shows no reflection of the finger wearing it. The blue-silver edge-light it carries is faint enough to miss in daylight.

wondrous.name: Amulet of Health
wondrous.description: A disc of Meridian Amber on a cord — the inclusions inside drift visibly over minutes, suspended in what should be rigid solid. When worn against skin it runs warm, and the cold violet light that traces the amber's edge is the same temperature as the body it touches.

wondrous.name: Boots of Speed
wondrous.description: Constructed from hide and a laminate sole material in alternating layers that shouldn't produce a flexible boot — the sole doesn't compress when pressed, yet the boot flexes naturally at the ball. Cold violet light sits at the ankle seam, dim enough to ignore until it moves when the wearer is standing still.

wondrous.name: Wand of Magic Missiles
wondrous.description: A rod of Weftglass, dark grey-green and slightly translucent — it casts a shadow with two extra edges that have no corresponding surface on the wand itself. The blue-silver luminescence at the tip pulses unevenly, as if counting something you can't hear.

legendary.name: Vorpal Sword
legendary.specialAbility: On a natural 20, target must make DC 15 CON save or be beheaded (instant death)
legendary.description: The edge is wrong — not sharp in a way a whetstone produces, but absent, a boundary where steel ends and something else begins, radiating a deep amber heat that casts no light but feels like standing too close to a forge. It predates the current Verge settlements by an interval no archivist will put a number on.

legendary.name: Armor of Invulnerability
legendary.description: Full plate in a metal with a density banding visible in cross-section at every cut edge — dark striations running against the hammer-work grain, as if two materials were resolved into one without either yielding. The deep amber heat distortion that hovers at the surface is faint but continuous, the kind of warmth that has no source and doesn't dissipate.
